reuse.why: Builds on the existing getWorstCaseAmount and the shared getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance helper from shared/rules instead of recomputing 7.5%, though sites keep their own null->0 ternary rather than using getScheduledAmount which already handles missing amounts.

duplication.why: The approx rule is written once in getExpectedAmount; the remaining repetition (null->0 at each site, and getExpectedAmount overlapping getScheduledAmount) is mostly pre-existing.

placement.why: The planning rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getWorstCaseAmount, where the tree keeps schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Touches only the amount-planning sites, a focused test and a release note.

maintainability.why: One function owns the rule, but getScheduledAmount gains an optional op that none of its callers pass and schedule-template.ts keeps a redundant op dispatch around the call.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All server planning sites (schedule-template, forecast normalizeSchedule, schedules/app updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, preview transactions) call getExpectedAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: No logic is copied in reshaped form; getExpectedAmount delegates to getWorstCaseAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold.

one_place.where: getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts; getScheduledAmount delegates to it, though its existing callers (api-models expectedAmount, desktop-client views) do not pass the op so they keep the exact value.
